title: Confined space entry protocol
summary: We enforce a strict sequence of ventilation, then gas testing with defined thresholds, periodic re-testing, and double guardian staffing for confined spaces.

content.overview: Our confined space work follows the mandatory 'ventilate, detect, then enter' principle, with precise gas concentration limits and frequent re-testing to maintain a safe atmosphere, supported by two or more dedicated attendants per shift.
content.details: Gas testing is done within 30 minutes before entry: O₂ must be 19.5%–23.5%, combustible gas <10% LEL, H₂S <10 mg/m³, CO <30 mg/m³. Continuous ventilation remains during occupancy. We re-test every 2 hours and immediately after any interruption. We require at least two attendants per entry shift to ensure rescue readiness and communication redundancy. This exceeds typical single-guardian practices because confined space rescues are high-risk and require immediate backup.
content.examples: Pre-entry gas readings logged: O₂ 20.9%, LEL 3%, H₂S 2 ppm, CO 5 ppm ↔ all passes. Attendants: one at entry point, one at communication station.
content.references: Confined space permit procedure, GB 50484-2019, company HSE manual.
content.caveats: Gas detectors must be bump-tested daily. If any gas concentration exceeds limit during work, immediate evacuation is required. Attendants must never enter for rescue without proper PPE and authorization.
